clauses.statement: The total second-kind numerator has zero order zero, constant original mass at order one, degree at most n-1, and the monic three-term numerator recurrence.
The numerator is the actual functional polynomial divided difference and, for a positive compactly supported real measure, its actual complex Bochner divided-difference integral.
Associated monic polynomials have exactly their order as degree and obey the recurrence with an arbitrary fixed coefficient shift; the numerator is original mass times the first associated sequence.

The numerator/denominator ratio is the Gauss partial fraction over any scalar field extension; the actual canonical Gauss weights are the numerator divided by the denominator derivative at their distinct nodes.
The native Stieltjes error is exactly rho_n/pi_n and exactly the squared-monic-norm Cauchy integral divided by pi_n squared, with denominator nonvanishing proved from support exclusion.
The quantitative finite moment-matching estimate is 2 times original mass times R^(2n)/(norm(z)^(2n)*(norm(z)-R)), giving the advertised order at infinity.

For infinite compact support the actual ratios converge to the native transform uniformly on every compact complex set outside the support enclosure; at finite-support termination the ratio already equals the transform exactly.

Every actual real Hermitian matrix's scalar-extended resolvent has its spectral partial fraction at every complex point outside its actual spectrum. The actual canonical Jacobi first-coordinate resolvent gives the same second-kind ratio with the original measure mass included; away from the real axis the actual Jacobi recurrence gives its ordinary continued fraction.

A strictly positive pole-free denominator on a compact support enclosure constructs the actual reciprocal-density measure's canonical Gauss rule, whose multiplied weights are positive and whose rational numerator space is exactly integrated through degree 2n-1.
Any distinct-node rule exact for that rational numerator space is the actual Gauss rule of the reciprocal-density measure after dividing its weights, up to node permutation.

The fixed-denominator numerator space has a unique polynomial-plus-repeated-pole expansion; the polynomial degree bound is exactly d minus the total pole degree, including the zero polynomial part when both degrees agree.

Cleared numerator expansions evaluate to the actual principal-part rational functions at pole-free arguments, and the monic pole convention is exactly the source's repeated 1+zeta*X convention by explicit nonzero scalar factors.
The native rationally modified positive measure has the same polynomial moment functional as the actual inverse-weight functional multiplied by u.

For every numerator and denominator degree, the actual monomial constraint matrix has a nonzero normalization determinant under the finite modified square-positivity hypothesis, and its inverse coefficients compute u times the canonical modified monic polynomial.

The actual first-row monomial determinant has its exact nonzero signed normalization coefficient and gives the canonical modified polynomial by exact polynomial division, including order zero and repeated roots.

On the original lower-orthogonal subspace, min(n,m) inverse-moment rows recover all n rows. The actual original-basis compressed minor is nonzero, including m>n, and computes the finite original-basis expansion of the modified numerator.

The compressed first-row determinant has exactly degree u plus min(n,m) constraint rows, a proved nonzero normalization coefficient, and gives the canonical modified monic polynomial by exact polynomial division.
The actual modified recurrence coefficients are recovered from consecutive modified monic next coefficients and from the original-measure rationally weighted squared-norm ratios at positive orders.
